audit.whatIsWrong: Spirit's Refuge is mentioned in nine strings and never once described correctly. The entry treats it as a blanket damage-denial zone — "if Spirit's Refuge is up your empowered autos get eaten, so feint the engage, wait the zone out, then commit", "Bait Spirit's Refuge with a feint, wait the zone out", "only trade when Spirit's Refuge is down".
audit.why: Riot's text is one sentence: "Attacks that would hit Shen or his allies near his spirit blade are blocked." It blocks ATTACKS. Cunning Sweep, Sundering Slam, Lacerate and Repudiation all land through it at full value — the only thing it takes away is the empowered auto. So the correct play is the opposite of waiting the zone out: keep casting inside it and hold the auto until it drops. Told to disengage for the full duration, the reader hands Shen a free 16-second reset every time, which is most of why the entry then concludes he out-sustains them.
audit.corrected: Restated as attack-block-only in spikes[0], early, mid, wants.you[2], wants.foe[0], whys[1], whys[2], dontsFull[1], dosFull[2] and report[5], with the instruction inverted to cast through it and save the auto.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] says Public Execution "suppresses through his flash" and mid says it "suppresses through a flash-react".
audit.why: Whether Public Execution's suppression lands through or beats a Flash react is not answerable from the kit files — champ-data/_kits/ambessa.json lists flashBuffer as unresolved, which means unknown, not yes. Stating it as fact is exactly the kind of claim a reader will bet a 130-second ultimate on. The verifiable reason the level-6 all-in works is simpler and better: Shadow Dash is his only interrupt and it is 18s at rank 1, so a baited taunt leaves him with nothing to break the chain.
audit.corrected: Flash claims removed from both strings and replaced with the Shadow Dash cooldown window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Four strings credit Public Execution with "R-passive armor pen" and "heal-on-ability-damage" / "R's heal-on-ability-damage tops you off" — spikes[1], spikes[2], mid and whys[4].
audit.why: Public Execution blinks to the farthest enemy champion in a line, suppresses on arrival, then slams for damage and a stun. No penetration and no healing; Drakehound's Step grants bonus attack range, damage, attack speed and an energy refund. Against Shen specifically the invented heal is the worst kind of wrong, because the entry uses it to justify extending a trade against a champion whose Q scales off your maximum health.
audit.corrected: Replaced with the suppress, the crash stun and the Shadow Dash window.

audit.whatIsWrong: Ki Barrier and Twilight Assault's max-health scaling are never mentioned. The entry attributes his sustain vaguely to "Q-sustain" and "he just farms and shields".
audit.why: Riot's Ki Barrier text: "After casting a spell, Shen gets a shield. Affecting other champions reduces the cooldown of this effect." The shield is not Spirit's Refuge and it comes back off every cast, faster when he lands things on you — that is the real reason chip damage does not accumulate on him. And Twilight Assault deals "damage based on the target's max health", which means the longer the trade the worse it gets for Ambessa regardless of her own damage. Both change how long you should stand there.
audit.corrected: Ki Barrier written into spikes[2], early and wants.foe[0]; the max-health scaling written into mid as the reason to keep trades short.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart disagrees with its own whys[] at four stages. It gives Shen level 2 while whys[1] says "stay even and farm", gives Shen level 3 while whys[2] says the combo "out-trades his spirit-blade autos", gives Skill at level 6 while whys[4] calls it a guaranteed gap-close and kill, and gives Shen the first-item stage while whys[5] calls it "your hardest favor window".
audit.why: At 51.42% over 422 games Ambessa is marginally ahead, and the shape is clear: even at 1-2, hers from 3 through first item, his once Spirit's Refuge and armour scale. The packet levelChart (Skill, Skill, Ambessa, Skill, Ambessa, Ambessa, Shen) matches the prose.
audit.corrected: Not changed. "Shen" is 4 characters, "Skill" 5, "Ambessa" 7, so every flip crosses the length band. Documented in notes.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[1].why repeats the champion-wide "Dash-resets stack your passive shield mid-trade" error, and no cooldown number appears in either layer despite Shadow Dash being the stated focus of the whole page.
audit.why: Drakehound's Step grants no shield. Shadow Dash is 18s at rank 1 falling to 10s, Spirit's Refuge 16s to 10s, Twilight Assault 8s to 5s, Stand United 200s. The 18s taunt is the number the entry is built around and it was never written down.
audit.corrected: phases[1].why corrected and real numbers written into spikes[1], spikes[3], mid, wants.you[1], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1], dosFull[2] and all three dontsFull descriptions are stock boilerplate that does not match their titles, and the three don't-strings are concatenated into report[11] as Common Mistakes.
audit.why: Each has a concrete answer: Shadow Dash is a 600-unit line you step off rather than outrun, Spirit's Refuge blocks attacks and not spells, and Stand United is a global shield-and-teleport on 200s.
audit.corrected: All five rewritten against the kit.

notes:
The Spirit's Refuge correction is the one that changes how the lane is played. Riot's text blocks attacks only, and the entry told the reader nine times to disengage for its whole duration — which against a 16-second cooldown means conceding most of the lane for no mechanical reason. Ambessa's abilities go through it untouched; only the Drakehound's Step empowered auto is denied.
